svg.aria-label: An isolation ladder with four rungs, from least to most isolated. Developer laptop, no sandbox: commands run with every file and credential on the machine. Antigravity terminal sandbox: commands confined to the workspace with no network by default and secrets such as ~/.ssh and .env blocked, but still on the laptop. Cloud Workstations: a dedicated VM per developer in a private cluster, reached through a private gateway, with no public VM IP addresses, a VPC Service Controls perimeter and a minimal service account, which keeps company credentials off laptops. GKE Agent Sandbox: a kernel-isolated Pod per run from a warm pool, with internal traffic and the metadata server blocked, for agent-generated code at scale. A side note says every rung still needs least-privilege credentials and human review before code ships.

g.text: Where a coding agent's code runs: the isolation ladder
A kernel-isolated Pod (gVisor or microVM) per run, from a warm pool.
Template Pods block internal ranges and metadata; restrict public egress.
A VM per developer in a private cluster: private gateway, no public VM IPs, VPC-SC.
Company credentials off laptops; the agent acts as a minimal service account.
Commands confined to the workspace; no network by default; ~/.ssh, .env blocked.
Still on the laptop, beside whatever credentials it holds.
Commands run with every file and credential on the machine.
Fine for reading code; risky for running what the agent wrote.
or Request Review if no sandbox
Every rung still needs least-privilege credentials, and human review before code ships.
